entries.def: (= they come out/are published every day)
(= short articles and lots of pictures)
(= pieces of writing about news items, e.g. a report in The Times)
(= pieces of writing about an important subject, e.g. an article about drugs)
(= title in large letters above the report/article, e.g. a front-page headline)
(= articles giving an opinion of new films, books, etc., e.g. a review of ...)
(= words and pictures about a product, to make people buy it, e.g. an ad for ...)
(= person in control of the daily production)
(= people who report news and write articles)
(= people who take the pictures in the papers)

entries.example: Government in new row over schools
Bush backs new law (= Bush has backed a new law)
British Rail chairman to quit (= the chairman is going to quit)
UN in bid to end war
Government and IRA in new talks
Bank of England cuts rate again

entries.word: It said in The Times that
entries.example: It said in The Times that they've found the missing girl. (NOT it's written in ...)
According to The Guardian, the missing girl was found last night.

note: Presentation is sections A–E on left page; entries are bold headwords with printed (= ...) glosses; Headlines table gives gloss + example headline. Exercises page excluded.
